stories.title: Google DeepMind releases Gemini 4 Neon, a mid-tier model aimed at coding agents and science work
paragraphs: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini 4 Neon on Nov. 18, 2026, describing it as a model that brings frontier-level intelligence with fast end-to-end task completion across software engineering, knowledge work and science workflows. MarkTechPost reports that Neon sits between Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Hydrogen in the Gemini 4 family, and that according to the model card it is adapted from Carbon. Google lists a price of $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, with a 1 million-token context window.

According to Google DeepMind, Neon scores 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its highest thinking level, ranking third overall, and ranks first on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index with 58.6. Google also reports 70.5% on Terminal-Bench Science, 84.0% on RiemannBench and 71.3% on HLE-Diamond. MarkTechPost stresses that these comparison scores are reported by Google, not independently reproduced, and notes that Claude Opus 5.5 still leads on Terminal-Bench 4.1 and FrontierCode 2.0.

Google says Neon is rolling out in the Gemini API in Google AI Studio, in Gemini for business, in Google Antigravity for paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers, and in the Gemini app for Pro and Ultra subscribers. A version called Gemini 4 Neon for cyber is rolling out to trusted defenders in the coming days, according to the post.

Simon Willison writes that the lineup's pricing is confusing for now: Carbon is temporarily at a discounted $2 and $10, which makes Neon the most expensive of the three models until Carbon's price doubles to $4 and $20 on Dec. 1. He adds that in his own drawing test Neon's output looked better than Hydrogen's and worse than Carbon's.

stories.title: Google adds Tool Retrieval to the Gemini API so agents load tool details only when needed
paragraphs: Google launched Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API on Nov. 19, 2026, available in preview in the Interactions API. In a post by Gemini API product manager Lucia Loher and Google DeepMind research scientist Nora Kassner, Google says that when an agent connects to dozens or hundreds of tools, sending every tool's full parameter description with each request inflates input token counts, adds latency and lowers tool-selection accuracy as the list grows.

With the feature, developers add a tool_search tool to a request and mark tools to hold back with defer_loading. According to Google, the model still sees each deferred tool's name and description, but its parameter details stay out of context until the model asks for that tool by name; the API then loads the details and the model calls the function, all inside the same request. Google says the search runs on its servers, so there is no index to build or host, and the feature also works with remote MCP servers.

Developers who keep their own tool registry or permission filters can instead run the search on their side, which Google says adds one round trip per search. The company says Tool Retrieval has no separate charge: tokens are billed at the model's standard rates, turning it on adds a small fixed block of input tokens, and each loaded tool description is billed as input for the rest of the conversation. Google says it works with Gemini 3.6 and later models, including all Gemini 4 models.

stories.title: Anthropic prices its initial public offering at $83 per share
paragraphs: Anthropic announced on Nov. 18, 2026, that it priced the initial public offering of its Class A common stock at $83.00 per share. According to the company, the offering consists of 980,000,000 shares, of which 956,351,354 are being sold by Anthropic and 23,648,646 by certain selling stockholders; Anthropic says it will not receive proceeds from the shares sold by those stockholders.

The company said the shares were expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Nov. 19, 2026, under the symbol "ANT," with the offering expected to close on Nov. 20, subject to customary closing conditions. Anthropic also granted the underwriters a 30-day option to buy up to 147,000,000 additional shares.

According to the announcement, the Securities and Exchange Commission declared the registration statement for the shares effective on Nov. 18, 2026. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are listed as the contacts for copies of the final prospectus.
